question.prompt: Suppose there is a special key on a calculator that replaces the number \(x\) currently displayed with the number given by the formula \(\frac{1}{1 - x}.\) For example, if the calculator is displaying \(2\) and the special key is pressed, then the calculator will display \(-1\) since \(\frac{1}{1 - 2} = -1.\) Now suppose that the calculator is displaying \(5.\) After the special key is pressed \(100\) times in a row, the calculator will display

solutions.explanation:
Track the displays until the starting value returns. The first three presses give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{1-5}&=-\frac14,\\
\frac{1}{1-(-\frac14)}&=\frac45,\\
\frac{1}{1-\frac45}&=5.
\end{aligned}
\]
All three denominators are nonzero. Once \(5\) returns, the same rule produces the same three displays again, so every three presses return the calculator to \(5\). None of the displays in this cycle is \(1\), so every later press is also defined.

Since \(100=3\cdot33+1\), the first 99 presses complete 33 cycles. The final press changes \(5\) to \(-\frac14=-0.25\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Find a repeating cycle
